cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Recruit Them Twice
cards.instruction: Recruit them to your side, then reveal that the side, goal, or conflict is not what it first appeared to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come and help me clear the committee cupboard. Start with the minutes; I'll tell you what we're keeping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sure. Shall I throw out the old ones?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. Those show three years of postponed repairs. You'll read the dates while I ask for a new committee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I agreed to clear a cupboard, not help you remove people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose now: leave me the minutes and stay out of the vote, or stand beside me and read them. We're deciding what this committee has been keeping shut.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs tidying; A3 rules which minutes stay and assigns political evidence reading; A5 gives B a concrete alignment choice under A framing after B rejects the covert recruitment.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 proposed disposal to reveal the records real purpose; A5 uses B4 consent objection to offer informed participation or withdrawal.

relationship.evidence: B2 practical disposal question and B4 political boundary are plausible responses from a willing helper.

heightening.evidence: A5 turns B4 objection into an explicit side choice rather than pretending tidying consent already covered a vote.

specificity.evidence: A1 cupboard minutes and A3 postponed repairs make the changed goal concrete.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 keeping shut echoes cupboard but the literal minutes and vote carry the meaning without the metaphor.
